verses.1: Then Moses and Aaron went to Pharaoh and said to him, “This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Let My people go so that they may celebrate Me in the wilderness.”
verses.2: Pharaoh asked them, “Who is this LORD, that I should listen to His voice to let Israel go? I do not know the LORD, and I will not let Israel go.”
verses.3: They said to him, “The God of the Hebrews has called us to go a three-day journey into the wilderness, so that we may sacrifice to the LORD our God. Otherwise, He may strike us with plague or sword.”
verses.4: The king of Egypt said to them, “Why have you two, Moses and Aaron, caused the people to abandon their labor? Go back to your work.”
verses.5: Pharaoh continued, “Now, indeed, the people have grown numerous. You cannot let them take time off from their labor.”
verses.6: That day, Pharaoh gave orders to the overseers of the people and their taskmasters, saying,
verses.7: “You must no longer supply the people with straw for their bricks, as before. Let them go and gather straw for themselves.
verses.8: But you must not reduce the quota of bricks that they were making before. Do not take anything away from their labor, for they are idle—this is why they are saying, 'Let us go and sacrifice to our God.'
verses.9: Let the labor become heavier for these people so they will occupy themselves with it and not be distracted by false words.”
verses.10: The overseers and the taskmasters went out and said to the people, “This is what Pharaoh says: I will not give you straw.
verses.11: Go out yourselves and gather whatever straw you can find. But you must not reduce your brick quota in any way.”
verses.12: The people scattered throughout the land of Egypt to gather stubble for straw.
verses.13: The taskmasters kept pressing them, saying, “Complete your daily quota as before, when you had straw to work with.”
verses.14: The taskmasters of the Israelites, who were appointed by Pharaoh’s overseers, were beaten and asked, “Why have you not completed your brick quotas as you did yesterday and the day before?”
verses.15: The Israelite taskmasters came and cried out to Pharaoh, saying, “Why are you treating your servants like this?
verses.16: You give us no straw, yet you demand we make bricks. But look, your servants are being beaten, and your people are being treated unjustly.”
verses.17: Pharaoh said to them, “You are idle, that is why you say, 'Let us go and sacrifice to the LORD.'
verses.18: Go now and work. No straw will be given to you, but you must deliver the quota of bricks as before.”
verses.19: The taskmasters saw that it was going badly for them, saying, “You must not reduce the brick quota for each day.”
verses.20: When the Israelite taskmasters met Moses and Aaron, they stood to greet them as they came out from Pharaoh.
verses.21: They said to them, “May the LORD look on you and judge you, for you have made the stench of our lives unbearable in the sight of Pharaoh and in the sight of his servants, giving him a sword in his hand to kill us.”
verses.22: Moses returned to the LORD and said, “Lord, why have You made things so bad for this people? Why have You sent me?
verses.23: Since I came to Pharaoh to speak in Your name, things have only gotten worse for this people, and You have not rescued Your people at all.”

notes:
Notes  
- v. 7: The Hebrew "תֶּֽבֶן" (tsemen) is translated as "straw" per context, not "flax." The Greek uses "ἄχυρον" (achuron), meaning "straw," aligning with the likely reading.  
- v. 17: The Greek uses "σχολάζετε" (scholaze) meaning "idle," which aligns with the Hebrew "נִרְפִּים" (nirpim), also meaning "idle" or "lazy."  
- v. 23: The Hebrew phrase "הֵרַע לָעָם הַזֶּה" (hera’ la’am haze) is translated as "made things so bad for this people," aligning with the Septuagint's "ἐκάκωσεν" (ekakōsen), meaning "made bitter."
